daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo will name potential successors to Gibran after returning from the ASEAN and APEC summits, with several names emerging as possible vice-presidential candidates. Regional Gerindra chapters have begun mobilizing support, with branches in Aceh, South Sumatra, and West Sumatra endorsing DPR Speaker Sufmi Dasco Ahmad for the position. Prabowo reportedly gave political parties one week to consider their nominations.

  • President Prabowo met party leaders at Bogor Palace to discuss coalition matters, with the Democrat Party revealing details of the meeting.
  • PKS announced it will not propose a vice-presidential candidate name, stating respect for Prabowo's coalition parties, while PKB emphasized the need for a candidate with extensive experience working with Prabowo and Golkar said it is still deliberating on its nomination.
  • Gerindra's Habiburokhman urged the MPR to proactively coordinate preparations for the vice-presidential election.
  • President Prabowo praised new National Police Chief Gen. Suyudi with what was described as a "proud greeting," and later Mahfud MD stated that the president was not close to Suyudi and that God had guided the revelation of major crimes.
  • President Prabowo opened the Muhammadiyah Tanwir conference attended by the Home Affairs Minister and national figures, where he praised the National Police Chief and said "finally the state is saved," while also urging Muhammadiyah to counter disinformation on campuses.
  • Prabowo announced he will earmark an additional Rp100 billion for each provincial capital and redirect state budget savings to regional development.
  • DPR Commission I requested assistance for Islamic boarding school students who were victims of abuse by TNI personnel, while the Army issued an apology and said the soldiers would be prosecuted, and a legislator called the action barbaric and demanded strict punishment.
  • Gerindra politician Habiburokhman promised to expel the Kupang Regent, a Gerindra cadre, if proven guilty of raping a university student, while DPR Commission III chair warned there should be no special treatment in the case.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo attended the opening of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila where he was welcomed by President Marcos, with Foreign Minister Tata using the summit as an opportunity to introduce herself as Indonesia's new foreign minister. Indonesia reaffirmed its commitment to reinforcing ASEAN unity and centrality at the summit. The ASEAN Summit agenda will include discussion of forest and land fires affecting the region.

  • Foreign Minister Tata met with her Singapore and Malaysian counterparts and reaffirmed Indonesia's commitment to resolve the forest fires issue.
  • Indonesia and Australia seek to strengthen regional disaster resilience cooperation.
  • The Indonesian Navy foiled the smuggling of 684 kg of tin sand in Riau Islands.
  • The Turkish Ambassador urged implementation of the Indonesia-Turkey MoU on climate cooperation.

Other

Indonesia has an opportunity to host COP33, with the Ministry of Environment revealing the challenges involved, while the country supports the COP31 BRIDGE Initiative and urges flexible financing for climate projects. Rising tourist arrivals in Lombok are creating job opportunities according to a minister. The Ministry is boosting synergy for the 2028 mandatory halal certification roadmap.

  • BULOG and Bapanas strengthened synergy to distribute food assistance in South Sulawesi, while Prabowo targeted 2,000 fishing villages by the end of 2027.
  • The government granted social forestry rights to 309 households in Sulawesi.
  • Bank Indonesia launched KAK Mart to expand market access and strengthen SMEs in East Nusa Tenggara.
  • A health ideology model based on Pancasila was officially launched, emphasizing public participation.
  • The poverty rate in Pohuwato declined significantly to 13.35 percent.
